2.  **Constraints on consecutive good partitions**:
    - If $k$ and $k+1$ are good partitions with the same value $X$, then $L_{k+1} = \text{lcm}(L_k, a_{k+1}) = \text{lcm}(X, a_{k+1}) = X$ implies $a_{k+1} \mid X$.
    - $G_k = \text{gcd}(a_{k+1}, G_{k+1}) = \text{gcd}(a_{k+1}, X) = X$ implies $X \mid a_{k+1}$.
    - Thus, $a_{k+1} = X$. Since the sequence $a_i$ is strictly increasing, $a_{k+1} = X$ can happen at most once for a fixed $X$. This means there can be at most two consecutive good partitions for any value $X$.
    - If $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ are good partitions with different values $X_i < X_{i+1}$, then $g_{j+1} \geq g_j + 2$. This is because $g_{j+1} = g_j + 1$ would imply $X_i = X_{i+1}$ (as shown in the derivation).

    - Let $m$ be the number of distinct values of $X_k$ across the 2015 good partitions.
